decisions.rationale: All 222 comparators were reviewed. The listed items share approval, Ask-flow, invocation, or ownership contracts, but Assistant Chat is a specific consumer boundary, so their authority and lifecycle are broader or different and none is merge-equivalent.

All 222 comparators were reviewed. Browser authority, action envelopes, tool ownership, and reader boundaries are adjacent, but none has the same rendering-source authority, preview trust tiers, product-surface boundary, and failure semantics.

All 222 comparators were reviewed. The listed container and Kubernetes features define discovery, commands, approvals, and mutation recovery; the anchor instead concerns the unresolved product-scope boundary and scale, so these are related members rather than equivalents.

All 222 comparators were reviewed. Effective-state disclosure, dynamic controls, and normalized routing are neighboring command concerns, but they do not duplicate the panel-consumer rule that canonical ownership and blocked/requested/effective semantics remain product-wide.

All 222 comparators were reviewed. These items expose attribution, account-reference, interface, or command-field gaps, but none covers the same goal-runtime actor, role, provider, model, and account reference schema boundary as the anchor.

All 222 comparators were reviewed. The listed scrub, disclosure, rendering, manifest, and capture concerns are plausible neighbors, but the anchor owns browser-artifact manifest schema and redaction-state enforcement; the comparators own different consumers or lifecycle stages.

All 222 comparators were reviewed. Command expansion, filesystem settings, projection, imports, and web URL safety share untrusted locator vocabulary, but they have distinct authorities and operations from artifact relative_path and source_url validation.

All 222 comparators were reviewed. These comparators concern attribution, export manifests, debug manifests, output references, or tool ownership, but none duplicates the producer, workspace owner, authorization, audience, and responsible-consumer boundary missing from the GUI automation manifest root.

All 222 comparators were reviewed. Fallback decisions, deny cascades, scheduler wakeup, and runtime recovery share concurrency hazards, but each has a different command authority or transition boundary from atomic blocked-episode resolution.

All 222 comparators were reviewed. Audit identity, recovery audit, sensitive provenance, and export minimization have adjacent privacy requirements, but they govern different records and lifecycle owners from durable approval provenance.

All 222 comparators were reviewed. The related items consume portions of HITL authority, identity, blocked state, or invocation consent; the anchor is the broader HITL owner/event/request/provenance/persistence contract, so umbrella/member merging is rejected.

All 222 comparators were reviewed. Approval surfaces, debug-state disclosure, debug expiry, and manifest ownership are members or adjacent consumers of the anchor's multi-unit boundary/surface/debug-grant bundle and therefore are not merge-equivalent.

All 222 comparators were reviewed. Permission precedence, hierarchy, and child inheritance are structurally related, but none defines the phase/task/subtask grouping-to-package-or-seam-gate mapping, precedence, deduplication, and mismatch behavior.

All 222 comparators were reviewed. Scope-key normalization, session invalidation, persistence tiers, lane isolation, and storage bleed are plausible neighbors, but none duplicates the durable cross-context scope-key privacy and isolation lifecycle.

All 222 comparators were reviewed. Wakeup, Ask-flow ownership, bounded HITL, and exact runtime recovery are downstream pieces, while the anchor is an umbrella over waits, recovery, action gating, labels, and shared permission consumption; member merging is rejected.

All 222 comparators were reviewed. Polling expiry, fallback approval states, scheduler wakeup, and debug-grant expiry share timer or race vocabulary, but none has the same approval-versus-expiry winner rule and exactly-once scheduler-wake lifecycle.

All 222 comparators were reviewed. These items cover scope identity, operation approvals, owner seams, blocked actions, recovery mappings, or resolution algorithms, but none supplies the same typed mapping between HITL runtime action families and the shared permission ladder.

All 222 comparators were reviewed. PF-0070 expresses the same Permissions-owned Ask-flow presentation seam and the same prohibition on local reinvention, matching authority, lifecycle, user outcome, state boundary, and failure semantics. PF-0056 and PF-0108 are broader propagation and invocation-consumer contracts.

All 222 comparators were reviewed. External-publication approval, teacher confirmation, and shared invocation consent are bounded decision mechanisms, but none owns the same classification boundary between auto-resolvable uncertainty and exceptional user-authority decisions.

All 222 comparators were reviewed. Composer blocking, mutation freshness, non-local action gates, and runtime recovery are related enforcement surfaces, but none duplicates PAUSE.md creator/validation/expiry/atomicity/race precedence and fail-safe semantics.

All 222 comparators were reviewed. Approval lifecycle, UI synchronization, permission replies, blocked payloads, and invocation results each overlap parts of the gap, but none is the same HITLRequest wire schema and complete request/response lifecycle.

All 222 comparators were reviewed. These items govern other destructive approvals, mutations, maintenance, terminal commands, or recovery dispatch, but the anchor specifically owns skip/abort runtime payload safety, stale-run guards, transactional effects, and compensation.

All 222 comparators were reviewed. Polling, fallback, wakeup, invocation timeout, timeout fields, and runtime recovery are adjacent, but none has the same per-HITL-request-kind timeout-to-cancel-or-skip mapping and late/duplicate response lifecycle.

All 222 comparators were reviewed. Approval UI state, accessible targets, compact permission surfaces, editor accessibility, and blocked notices are related members, but none spans the anchor's full HITL copy, redaction, accessibility, localization, stale/offline, support, metrics, and conformance boundary.

All 222 comparators were reviewed. Audit identities, sensitive provenance, invocation context, and provider provenance have adjacent data-lifecycle risks, but they are different records and consumers from the interview-to-runtime shared identity packet.

All 222 comparators were reviewed. These comparators disclose requested/effective permission or debug state, but the anchor governs presentation of interview/runtime identity summaries, mismatch indicators, redaction, staleness, accessibility, and localization; shared vocabulary does not make them equivalent.

All 222 comparators were reviewed. Attribution closure and dispatch-time freshness are related integrity controls, but none owns the prelaunch equality oracle among requested, effective, consumer, and launched-run identity fields or its repair path.

All 222 comparators were reviewed. Permission conflicts, indeterminate recovery, projection conflicts, and identity collisions are plausible neighbors, but none matches the durable interview-handoff conflict object, authorized resolution, resume persistence, and resolved audit transition.

All 222 comparators were reviewed. Cross-surface envelopes, blocked payload schemas, GoalRun interfaces, and invocation results share schema concerns, but none is the canonical interview handoff packet with its exact fields, referential integrity, trust, replay, and validation errors.

All 222 comparators were reviewed. Account-root import, provider-native adoption, and investigation-bundle import share untrusted-input and path concerns, but their imported objects, owners, transitions, and failure recovery differ from provider-native interview handoff forms.

All 222 comparators were reviewed. Bounded HITL lanes, child inheritance, and delegated-task contracts involve concurrency or child runs, but none defines Orchestrator reviewer reservation atomicity, cap exhaustion, fairness, cancellation release, and retry timing.

All 222 comparators were reviewed. These items distinguish governance or metadata proof from runtime proof, but none has the same document-title authority and direct contradiction between implementation-plan identity and summary-only status.

All 222 comparators were reviewed. Auth setup, route epochs, account-reference policy, egress, and provenance are adjacent, but none has the same provider-auth reconciliation invariants for failed, stale, revoked, unavailable, or requested/effective mismatch states.

All 222 comparators were reviewed. Attribution seams, Ask-flow ownership, Skills SSOT, and tool authority illustrate other owner boundaries, but none owns the package-local to seam-governance handoff, conflict precedence, triggers, partial failures, and consumers described by the anchor.

All 222 comparators were reviewed. Account isolation, setup/removal, route epochs, reference policy, and provider provenance are neighbors, but none defines the requested/effective multi-account switch transaction, concurrency, privacy, failure, and acceptance lifecycle.

All 222 comparators were reviewed. Remote disconnects, GoalRun consumers, tool authority, and action gates are adjacent integration concerns, but none duplicates the native workbench service-interface boundary, policy/error taxonomy, cancellation, and lost-control-plane behavior.

All 222 comparators were reviewed. Historical snapshots, generated-media provenance, and provider migration lineage are related, but none defines the qualifying lineage predicate that changes historical-run versus superseded-object classification and recovery.

All 222 comparators were reviewed. Scrubbing, browser permissions, rendering redaction, context sharing, action envelopes, and capture races are components or adjacent consumers; none spans the anchor's agent-preview navigation, untrusted-content, credential, destructive-action, network-loss, capture-redaction, and evidence-validity boundary.

All 222 comparators were reviewed. Explicit web operations, approval tiers, bounded batches, dispatcher parity, permission algorithms, and scalable review are members of the area, but none is the same compressed summary whose unnamed operations and ladder prevent independent falsification.

All 222 comparators were reviewed. Container discovery, command families, mutation recovery, exact approvals, and Kubernetes recovery are adjacent, but none defines Docker registry-management parity capabilities, credential lifecycle, destructive confirmation, scale bounds, and acceptance.

All 222 comparators were reviewed. GUI catalog separation, tool ownership, registry integration, and registry churn are related, but none duplicates the base-catalog plus settings-overlay authority, stable-ID merge precedence, and research-write boundary.

All 222 comparators were reviewed. Host resolution, bounded MCP degradation, schema-cycle isolation, and registry churn are close neighbors, but PF-0190 is a broader bundle and the others own different states; none matches the complete selection/enablement lifecycle across provider partial availability, auth, connectivity, identity change, denial, and adapter failure.

All 222 comparators were reviewed. Dynamic control identity and the broader UCC routing/gating envelope are related, but the latter is an umbrella and neither comparator is exactly the narrow rule that convenience view state cannot become operational route-target identity.

All 222 comparators were reviewed. Missing runtime oracles, exact metadata checks, Doctor semantics, and custom-tool safety are related, but none has the same contradiction between existence/executable metadata, actual tool execution, and canonical evidence production.

All 222 comparators were reviewed. Scrub gates, image disclosure, export minimization, display redaction, retention classes, and capture races are distinct lifecycle stages or consumers; none covers the full capture-to-render GUI evidence-media privacy, access, retention, deletion, export, consent, capacity, and accessibility lifecycle.

All 222 comparators were reviewed. Browser permission matrices, promotion, context sharing, action envelopes, and session races are plausible neighbors, but none matches attach-existing profile/tab isolation, reauthorization, unrelated-tab exclusion, and detach cleanup.

All 222 comparators were reviewed. Remote fallback, browser authority, dispatch failures, and freshness gates are related, but none defines the browser-auto preflight taxonomy separating safe availability fallback from trust, permission, integrity, version, or target failures that must block.

All 222 comparators were reviewed. Debug disclosure, browser authority, and action envelopes are adjacent, but none duplicates the ephemeral-debug-session default, attention_required handling for authenticated state, and undeclared-host preflight block.

All 222 comparators were reviewed. Redaction, teardown, and capture failure semantics are related, but none owns mobile device/simulator permission prompts, personal-data reset/isolation, degraded network and disconnect recovery, device matrices, and cleanup.

All 222 comparators were reviewed. Docker/Kubernetes command and recovery contracts are adjacent, but none duplicates the internal normative contradiction over whether Docker Compose failure gates build-only or publish entry points.

All 222 comparators were reviewed. External publication approval, notification recovery, container transactions, destructive maintenance, and Kubernetes partial failure are neighbors, but none owns the publish/Unraid payload lifecycle, digest reconciliation, crash recovery, stale-auth TTL, and partially committed template-repository state.
